messages.content: The museum confirmed the Thursday condition review. It starts at 9:30 a.m. and should finish around 1:00 p.m., so Wednesday is no longer an option. Please compare the Monday outbound and Thursday returns again.

For Monday, October 12, Southwest WN 2418 is still available nonstop from Atlanta at 1:20 p.m., arriving in St. Louis at 2:05 p.m. The current fare is $218, including your carry-on and checked supply case. Allowing about 35-50 minutes to reach Forest Park, you should be at the hotel around 3:15-3:35 p.m., with ample time to settle in and prepare for Tuesday's 8:00 a.m. report time.

For Thursday, Southwest WN 1740 departs at 2:50 p.m. and Delta DL 1284 departs at 4:15 p.m.; both are nonstop.
How realistic is the 2:50 flight if the review actually runs until 1:00?

It is too tight to recommend. Leaving the museum at 1:05 p.m., the drive to STL would normally take about 25-35 minutes, putting you at the terminal around 1:30-1:40. That leaves roughly 70-80 minutes before departure, with little protection against a late review, traffic, returning to collect luggage, or checking the supply case.

Delta DL 1284 at 4:15 p.m. leaves a much better margin. Even if the review ends at 1:15, you could collect your luggage and leave around 1:30, reach the airport near 2:05, and still have about two hours before departure.
What are the complete schedules and totals if I pair each return with the Southwest outbound?

Option 1: Southwest both ways. WN 2418 flies ATL-STL Monday from 1:20 p.m. to 2:05 p.m.; WN 1740 flies STL-ATL Thursday from 2:50 p.m. to 5:25 p.m. The round-trip total is now $442, with the checked supply case included.

Option 2: Southwest outbound and Delta return. WN 2418 has the same Monday schedule. DL 1284 flies STL-ATL Thursday from 4:15 p.m. to 6:48 p.m. The combined airfare is $461, including Delta's $35 checked-bag charge. Both itineraries are nonstop.
The extra $19 is worth not rushing after the review. Nonstop is the right choice for these museum trips when the schedule is fixed like this.
Agreed. The Delta return gives you a practical airport margin without adding a connection. Before I book it, should I use the traveler details and payment method already on file for Avery Thompson?
Yes. Book Southwest WN 2418 outbound and Delta DL 1284 back with the method on file.

I have the itinerary ready at the quoted $461 total: $218 for Southwest and $243 for Delta including the checked-bag fee. The tickets are separate, so there will be two confirmation codes. Shall I complete both purchases?

Both flights are ticketed. Southwest WN 2418 departs ATL Monday, October 12 at 1:20 p.m. and arrives STL at 2:05 p.m. Southwest confirmation: L8Q2RM.

Delta DL 1284 departs STL Thursday, October 15 at 4:15 p.m. and arrives ATL at 6:48 p.m. Delta confirmation: H6T9VK. The total charged was $461, including the checked supply case on the return.
Confirm the Thursday timing one more time, including when I should leave the museum.

With the review scheduled to end around 1:00 p.m., collect your stored luggage and plan to leave the Forest Park museum by 1:30 p.m. The drive to STL is generally 25-35 minutes, so you should reach the terminal around 2:00 p.m., about 2 hours 15 minutes before the 4:15 p.m. departure. Even a 15-minute overrun would still leave a reasonable margin for checking the supply case and clearing security.
Good. Give me the final booked itinerary in one concise record.

Booked for Avery Thompson, October 12-15. Outbound: Southwest WN 2418, Monday, ATL 1:20 p.m. to STL 2:05 p.m., confirmation L8Q2RM. Return: Delta DL 1284, Thursday, STL 4:15 p.m. to ATL 6:48 p.m., confirmation H6T9VK. Total charged: $461, including the checked supply case. After Thursday's 9:30 a.m.-1:00 p.m. condition review, retrieve the stored luggage and leave the museum by 1:30 p.m. for a planned airport arrival around 2:00 p.m.
